Only their combination yields the one-sided bound needed for the all-zero Lehmer criterion.

items.proposed_content: At a simple real zero, the two-variable equation H_t(x)=0 can be resolved locally as a differentiable zero trajectory x(t). Differentiating that identity turns local derivatives of H_t into a velocity description. The lemma makes the zero locally trackable, not reversible, and it does not apply at a multiple zero or determine whether any pair collides.

items.proposed_content: The span gives two complementary descriptions of H_t: threshold-side membership in the Laguerre-Polya class expresses the real-zero condition as a class criterion, while even Hadamard factorization replaces the function by modulus-ordered zero coordinates with finite reciprocal-square mass. The second description preserves the zero multiset and the stated summability control but omits the original integral kernel; it does not supply later inequalities or closure arguments.

This makes the example locally identifiable in the paper's chosen coordinates; any later analytical use is preparatory inference, not a result proved in this span.

items.proposed_content: A Lehmer pair is not defined by a small raw gap alone: its squared gap is normalized by a convergent interaction involving all other zeros. Thus the surrounding zero configuration is part of the static criterion. Evenness and real-entire symmetry make the aggregate real even if hypothetical nonreal zeros occur, but this unit does not yet assign the sum a heat-flow force or collision meaning.

In this span I and R are not yet defined or bounded, so the decomposition organizes the remaining proof burden but the local sum alone is neither a dominance result nor a Lehmer certificate.

Because the leading gap-squared term dominates the displayed lower-bound expansion, the source tests the final, smallest listed gap first and then still requires the full Lehmer condition; early record gaps demonstrate that record status is not sufficient for Lehmer-pair status.
